questions.q: Why does every staging model in this platform start from a declared source() rather than a bare table name?
options: dbt does not allow querying a raw table by its literal name under any circumstances
A declared source() is what makes the raw table resolve anywhere in the project and show up as a node in the lineage graph
source() is only required for tables with more than 1,000 rows
It makes the model run faster at query time
questions.explain: The sources .yml file declares the raw table so source('jaffle_shop', 'raw_orders') resolves consistently and appears in the lineage graph Lesson 14 generates.

questions.q: Why is the naming convention stg_jaffle_shop__orders rather than just stg_orders?
options: dbt requires double underscores in every model name
The source__table pattern disambiguates staging models once more than one source feeds staging models, which this platform adds in Chapter 5
Longer names make SQL run faster
Snowflake does not allow table names shorter than 20 characters
questions.explain: stg_<source>__<table> keeps two staging models from different sources instantly distinguishable at a glance, which matters once a second source exists.

questions.q: Which of the following belongs in a staging model, per this lesson's rules?
options: A join combining two different source tables
Renaming a column to a consistent, readable name and light type casting
Aggregating rows with a GROUP BY to compute a summary metric
Filtering out rows the business considers low-quality
questions.explain: Staging models are intentionally narrow: rename/cast only, one source table at a time — joins and aggregation are intermediate/mart work.

questions.q: Why does keeping staging models join-free and business-logic-free matter for Lesson 12's schema-change scenario?
options: It has no connection to schema changes at all
It's exactly what lets a late-breaking rename ripple through cleanly and predictably, instead of unpredictably through tangled logic
Join-free models run twice as fast in Snowflake
It only matters for Power BI performance, not for schema changes
questions.explain: A narrow staging layer is precisely what contains a schema-change blast radius to one predictable spot, as Lesson 12 later demonstrates.

questions.q: In the raw_orders staging plan, which raw column becomes customer_id in stg_jaffle_shop__orders?
options: id
user_id
order_date
status
questions.explain: raw_orders.user_id is renamed to customer_id in the staged model, matching the planned column list in this lesson.
